key_insight: Corrosion significantly degrades the ultra-low-cycle fatigue resistance of Q355 steel welded joints, motivating a cyclic constitutive model that captures their damaged response.
engineering_relevance: The findings are directly relevant to durability design and remaining-life assessment of welded steel connections exposed to marine, industrial, or other corrosive environments.
method: Tested Q355 steel welded joints under corrosion conditions and cyclic loading.
Analyzed ultra-low-cycle fatigue performance to characterize degradation behavior.
Developed a cyclic constitutive model for the corroded welded joints.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates a journal-article study focused on experimental performance evaluation plus constitutive modeling, though it does not report numerical results in the provided text.
watch_item: The model should be validated carefully across corrosion levels, weld types, and loading histories before using it for design extrapolation.
paper_title: Ultra-low cycle fatigue performance and cyclic constitutive model of Q355 steel welded joints under corrosion conditions
